brief.offer: Video case studies with engineering teams that use your product

facts.claim: Tuple makes a remote pair-programming app for macOS and Windows.
facts.excerpt: The best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows

facts.claim: The app supports mouse and keyboard input for both participants, command-line integration, and pluginability.
facts.excerpt: Seamless collaboration with full-time mouse and keyboard support for both parties, snappy interactions, command-line integration and pluginability.

facts.claim: Tuple has a Slack integration that starts pairing sessions from a channel or direct message.
facts.excerpt: Tuple's integration for Slack adds a `/tuple` command, which will start a pairing session directly from a channel or DMs.

facts.claim: Tuple’s Slack integration lets coworkers see participants’ busy status.
facts.excerpt: Participants will also have their Slack status changed, so that your coworkers know you're busy.

facts.claim: Tuple is headquartered in Somerville, Massachusetts.

research.website_note: The results identify tuple.app as Tuple’s official site and link Tuple’s GitHub organization to tuple.app.
research.gaps: The results do not establish Tuple’s pricing, customer names, or current business priorities.

strategy.observation: Tuple supports shared mouse and keyboard input for both participants, along with command-line integration and pluginability.
strategy.offer_link: Video case studies with engineering teams could show how those collaboration features work in real development workflows, giving Tuple concrete customer evidence to use in marketing.
hypotheses: Tuple may want more customer proof that explains how engineering teams use these features.
Some teams using Tuple may be willing to take part in a video case study.
strategy.angle: Tuple’s shared mouse-and-keyboard input and command-line integration make for a specific engineering workflow to bring to life in a customer case study.
strategy.fit_reason: The offer directly supports marketing for a product whose value is expressed through how engineering teams work with it; the facts do not confirm whether Tuple needs case studies or has customers available to participate.

draft.subject: Showcasing Tuple workflows
draft.body:
Tuple’s shared mouse-and-keyboard input and command-line integration give an engineering team a specific workflow to show in a customer story. If you’re looking to add customer proof around how those features work in practice, a video case study could make that workflow clear to other teams.

I produce video case studies with engineering teams that use your product. Do you have a customer in mind who might be open to showing a real pairing session on video?
